text: KARSTOV, Nov. 13 — The Voskresen manuscript was written in Old Church Slavonic, people familiar with the matter said Thursday, ending weeks of debate among paleographers at the Orlov Archive. The attribution was confirmed after carbon dating of the birch-bark binding and a new ink analysis tied the text to a 12th-century monastic scriptorium near Lake Veyna. Archivist Lena Mirov said the language identification matched a set of liturgical phrases and marginal notes long misread as regional dialect. The 84-page codex, first cataloged in 1998, will return to controlled storage next week after a public viewing drew more than 1,200 visitors, the people said.
